title: Engine segfaults on exit if a CanvasTexture RID is leaked
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.4.stable, 4.5.stable, 4.6.stable, 4.7.stable, 4.7.1.stable, 4.7.2.stable
- Not reproducible in: 4.0.stable, 4.1.stable, 4.2.2.stable, 4.3.stable. The CanvasTexture still leaks in those, the engine just exits cleanly.

### System information

macOS 27.0 - Godot v4.7.2.stable - Forward+ (Metal 4.0) - Apple M3 Pro

### Issue description

If a CanvasTexture RID is still allocated when the engine shuts down, Godot segfaults instead of just printing the usual `RID allocations of type ... were leaked at exit`.

I ran into it with a dual-grid TileMapLayer addon that leaks a TileSet along with its CanvasTextures. The editor crashed every time I closed it, restarted it, or went back to the project list, and it took me a while to connect that to the leak. The MRP does the same thing the simple way: drops a Sprite2D out of the tree without freeing it.

The cleanup loop in `~RID_Alloc` destroys the leaked elements, so `~CanvasTexture` runs and fires its `invalidated_callback`. That callback belongs to `RendererCanvasRenderRD`, which is already gone by then: `RendererCompositorRD::finalize()` deletes the canvas renderer before the texture storage, so `RendererCanvasRender::singleton` is null and the callback dereferences null. `~RendererCanvasRenderRD` does clear this callback for `default_canvas_texture`. Just not for anything in `canvas_texture_to_uniform_set`.

Side effect: the crash lands before the ObjectDB leak dump, so the `Leaked instance:` lines that would tell you what leaked never print. On `gl_compatibility` the same project leaks the CanvasTexture and exits fine.

I have a fix for this and will open a PR.
### Steps to reproduce

1. New project, Node2D main scene, attach this script:

```gdscript
extends Node2D

var sprite: Sprite2D
var frames: int = 0

func _ready() -> void:
      var texture := CanvasTexture.new()
      texture.diffuse_texture = GradientTexture2D.new()
      sprite = Sprite2D.new()
      sprite.texture = texture
      sprite.position = Vector2(200, 200)
      add_child(sprite)

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
      frames += 1
      if frames == 30:
              remove_child(sprite) # never freed, so it and its CanvasTexture leak
      if frames > 60:
              get_tree().quit()
```

2. Run it. The sprite has to be drawn before it's removed, since the callback is only registered while batching a CanvasTexture.
3. It quits itself after 60 frames and crashes with signal 11 on the way out.

Run it from the project directory and check the exit code: 134 on 4.4 and later, 0 on 4.3.

```sh
godot; echo $?
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[canvas_texture_leak_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31265859/canvas_texture_leak_mrp.zip)
